The working file is the complete analysis; the Markdown and PDF reports are reader copies of it. Each should be read in full — this message is only a pointer, not the analysis.

In brief: leadership's "deploys are too slow → we need microservices" is a non-sequitur (HIGH confidence) — the 45-minute pipeline and coordinated restart are properties of this org's CI/test/deploy mechanics, not of being a monolith, and the Rails ecosystem already ships tooling (built-in parallel testing) built to fix exactly that without any service split. The organizational benefit microservices actually deliver (independent team release cadence, Conway's-Law-aligned boundaries) requires per-service owning teams that 12 engineers across four tightly-coupled domains don't have, while splitting checkout/fulfillment now adds real, avoidable distributed-consistency risk. Recommendation (MEDIUM confidence overall): run a sequenced bundle — test tiering, parallel test sharding, rolling/zero-downtime deploys, then modular-monolith boundaries — gated by a short profiling spike, and defer any service extraction until the team-size and modular-design thresholds identified in the analysis are actually met.
